name: Tahath
overview: Tahath was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a Kohathite. He is uniquely noted as the son of Assir, situating him within the Levitical genealogies. His role and identity are grounded in the priestly lineage, reflecting the importance of the tribe of Levi in Israel's worship and service.
namesAndTitles: The name Tahath means 'compensation,' a proper name recorded in Scripture but not indicated as given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a concept of restitution or balance, though the biblical text does not elaborate further on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tahath as the son of Assir. It is also inferred that Uriel was his father, providing a generational link within the Levitical family. Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Tahath's significance lies in his place within the Kohathite branch of the Levites, a group entrusted with sacred duties related to the tabernacle. Being the son of Assir connects him to the priestly heritage that served God faithfully. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:24 anchors him within the biblical record of Israel's spiritual leaders and their genealogies.
